Commentary.Commentary: We have witnessed a nail biter today and the crowd got their full money worth. A great moment for a small cricketing nation to register a tie against a good West Indies side and definitely worth cherishing. We hope you enjoyed our coverage today. Join us for the 4th ODI between Zimbabwe and Sri Lanka on 21st November in Bulawayo (0930 local, 1300 IST). Till then, goodbye and take care!
Man of the Match, Shai Hope says that a hundred doesn't mean much if you don't win. Adds that the pitch had a bit of grip and the bowlers bowled really well.

Zimbabwe skipper, Graeme Cremer says that they made some mistakes in the second half and it could have gone their way. Adds that they fought back well. Mentions that they dropped a couple of catches. Feels that they were 15-20 runs short but it was a terrific effort from his boys.

West Indies skipper, Jason Holder says that he is disappointed. Feels that they should have won the game. Adds they need to learn a lot from this and hope it doesn't happen in future. Praises Hope who scored a great century and Kraigg Brathwaite as well for his handy knock. Credits the bowlers who bowled really well too.

Russell Tiffin gets a special award for standing in 150 ODIs. He becomes the first Zimbabwean to achieve this feat. He is felicitated by Zimbabwe Cricket. Don't forget this is the 200th ODI in Zimbabwe as well.

Earlier, Zimbabwe posted a decent total on the board after winning the toss, thanks to fifties from Craig Ervine and Sikandar Raza. The former missed out on his ton by just 8 runs. They could have posted more but some late wickets towards the end hampered their chances. Carlos Brathwaite was the pick of the bowlers for West Indies as he grabbed four wickets. The Windies lost a couple of wickets cheaply in their run chase but Shai Hope and Kraigg Brathwaite shared a superb 162-run stand which almost sealed the game. Zimbabwe were really quick with their over rate too, not to forget that. Their spinners were accurate and didn't really let West Indies score freely. Williams and Tiripano finished with two wickets each while Cremer and Mpofu got one apiece.

West Indies were 220 for three at one stage, 38 needed from 33 balls and with some hard hitters to follow, they were complete favourites. Shai Hope, the centurion's wicket sparked a collapse as West Indies lost quick wickets. All the batsmen got out in a bid to score quick runs. Donald Tiripano bowled a superb last over and didn't let the tourists win this encounter.

Unbelievable! We've witnessed a thriller here in Bulawayo! West Indies were cruising at one stage but Zimbabwe fought back hard and didn't let the visitors to win! Just the third Tie in Zimbabwe and first in 19 years. Amazing game of cricket! As they say, it's a game of glorious uncertainties.

The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fullish delivery on middle and off, defended to mid-wicket.
On a length straying on the pads, Charles works it towards short fine leg and sets off for the run. Brathwaite has to scamper across and if there was a direct hit, it would have been very close.
SIX! HIT WITH A LOT OF DISDAIN! Bowls a fuller one outside off, Charles extends his arms and hits it powerfully over mid on. The ball clears the fence.
Shortish delivery angling into the body, Charles swivels across and pulls it powerfully  behind square leg for a couple.
Length delivery outside off, Johnson strides forward and drives it to mid off.
Fuller length on off, pushed a bit uppishly back towards the bowler.
On a length angling in on off, Kraigg shuffles a bit and works it through square leg for a couple.
Back of a length ball outside off, Kraigg hangs back and defends it to the covers.
FOUR! SHOT! Shortish and wide outside off, Brathwaite camps back and cuts it fiercely through backward point and the ball races to the fence.
Angling in on middle and off, Kraigg clips it towards short mid-wicket.
On a length outside off, Brathwaite camps back and pushes it to the covers.
Donald Tiripano to bowl from the other end.
Slower one on middle and off, turned towards mid-wicket.
Back of a length ball outside off, Charles stays back and plays it to point.
Straying on the hips, tucked towards backward square leg.
Length delivery outside off, Brathwaite lunges and pushes it to the covers for a single.
Length delivery outside off, Charles camps back and steers it through backward point to get off the mark!
On a length wide outside off, Charles is not bothered to play at that.

We are back for West Indies' reply with the bat. The pitch is turning and keeping low at times. Can Zimbabwe defend this total? It is going to be an exciting chase. Kraigg Brathwaite and Johnson Charles to open the batting. Chris Mpofu to start with the new cherry.
